title: Account record
description: One entry of accounts.json. The file is a bare JSON array of these objects, matching the reference implementation's channels.json byte-for-byte in shape so an existing record can be migrated without hand-editing. REVISED 2026-10-04 for the PC (HD) flow - see 开发侧取证记录 'phase 3 protocol'. The record is derived from qrcode/query's login_info plus the exchange_token response; see svs_autologin/accounts.py. The Android-era keys (loginResp / bili_sdk_ver / top-level login_channel / game_id) are documented at the bottom as legacy: the PC chain has no uni_sauth step, so nothing writes them.

uuid.description: Stable identity key, and what the auto.<game_id> config value points at. Derived as '<login_info.login_channel>-<login_info.code>', e.g. 'bilibili_sdk-100001'. NOTE: there is NO channel prefix in the auto-scan path; the 'bili-bilibili_sdk-100001' form only comes out of the reference implementation's manual-import path, and a record carrying it keeps it (upsert inherits the previous uuid on a rescan).

name.description: Display name, shown in the account picker. Falls back to the uuid when empty - a record with no name still has to be selectable. Not a credential and not a uid.

login_info.description: The login_info object qrcode/query returns once the QR reaches status 2. Its login_channel and code are what the uuid is derived from, so it is required even though everything in it is channel-defined.

code.description: Channel-specific account code (bilibili: SESSDATA-derived). Part of the uuid.

login_channel.description: Which channel handler owns this account.

user_info.description: The 'user' object from the exchange_token response. THIS IS A CREDENTIAL - treat the whole file as a secret (docs/constraints.md C4). Both fields are required by svs_autologin/accounts.py: a record missing either makes get_uni_sdk_data raise '需要重新扫码授权' rather than sending a confirm_login that cannot succeed.

id.description: Channel uid, string-typed even when it looks numeric. The PRIMARY dedupe key: two records with different ids are different accounts even if their uuids collide, and upsert keeps them apart on purpose.

token.description: The session token, base64(sessionid) - not a plaintext sessionid. Sent verbatim as the confirm_login body's 'token' field. The value here is fabricated; real tokens never enter the repo (docs/constraints.md C4).

client_data.description: Opaque base64 blob, passed through untouched.

ext_info.description: The 'ext_info' object from the exchange_token response. Despite the name it is not optional in practice: every field of the confirm_login body except user_id/token is read from here (src_app_channel2, src_udid, src_app_channel, src_jf_game_id, src_pay_channel, extra_unisdk_data). A record without it still loads, but confirms with empty channel fields.

src_udid.description: Becomes the body's udid. NOT device_info.udid - see 开发侧架构拆解.

src_jf_game_id.description: Feeds BOTH the body's sdk_version and its jf_game_id. Deliberate fidelity to the reference implementation, which reads this one field twice; tests/test_accounts.py pins it so nobody 'fixes' it.

extra_unisdk_data.description: Forwarded verbatim as the body's extra_unisdk_data; not rebuilt locally. The SAUTH material for the PC chain lives inside this string, and the game reads it after its own exchange_token. This is why sauth.build_unisdk_result (which derives an equivalent blob from the record) is NOT used on the PC path.

device_info.description: The 'device' object from the exchange_token response, passed through opaquely. NOTE: the confirm_login body's udid comes from ext_info.src_udid, not from here.

create_time.description: Unix epoch seconds. Display only; not a credential and not used in any decision. Defaults to 0 when absent (the reference implementation defaults to 'now', which makes records non-reproducible).

last_login_time.description: Unix epoch seconds, refreshed only after mkey accepts a confirm_login. A stale value here is a claim that a login worked when it may not have - so a failed flow must leave it untouched. Also the tiebreak upsert uses to pick which duplicate's name/uuid to inherit.

_legacy_android_shape.description: SUPERSEDED, not written by the PC flow. Kept documented because svs_autologin/sauth.py still reads these keys when building an Android-era SAUTH payload (build_sauth_payload / build_unisdk_result), and tests/conftest.py's sample_account fixture still uses this shape.

keys.loginResp: Object with required uid + access_key, the result of the Android uni_sauth exchange. The PC chain has no uni_sauth step at all - the equivalent material arrives inside ext_info.extra_unisdk_data - so no PC record has this key.
keys.bili_sdk_ver: bilibili SDK version string; feeds the SAUTH sdk_version field on the Android path only.
keys.login_channel: Top-level channel name. The PC record keeps it inside login_info instead, so a top-level login_channel is a sign of a legacy record.
keys.game_id: The FULL id last used with this record. The PC flow never stores it: the id is per-login and comes from the live create_login query.
